124840.overview:
L'Aigle d'Or is an action-adventure game and the first episode of a series.

The location is Eagle's Castle in Westphalia. You start by buying equipment, such as a rope, for example. You can now start to explore the castle, room after room. It may be wise to draw a map, since the rooms look quite the same. In some of them, you'll discover secret passageways.
You move using the arrow keys and start actions using the first letter of the verb. For example, hit the "O" key to open a treasure chest. Collect items, keys and gold coins, use medicines if you need them, and beware of traps and monsters hidden in the castle. But remember, your aim is to find the Golden Eagle.

159829.overview:
This was an early interpretation of the Tron Light Cycles game style, in which the players (two on here, with the option of human or computer opposition) control a beam of light, which constantly extends as you move automatically. They must move it around an arena so as to cause their opponent's beam to crash into part of their's, or into the wall. This can be done by moving yours tightly around, so as to cram your opponent into a small space.

The control method of this version involves up, down, left and right controls, with instant death (and the resultant multi-colour display in the border) occurring from trying to double back on yourself, or hitting any part of your own beam. There are 7 speed level on offer.

175563.overview: Lone Raider is a Scramble clone for the Oric-1 and Atmos computers. It was developed by Adrian Sheppard and published by both Severn Software and  Infogrames in the UK and France respectively.

175614.overview: Le Retour du Dr Genius is a French language adventure game with graphics for the Oric computers. It was developed and published by Loriciels in 1984.

175618.overview: Le Sceptre d'Anubis is a French text-based adventure game with graphics set in the Pyramid of Djoser. The player takes a role of an experienced archeologist on vacation in Egypt, who occasionally discovered an ancient papyrus in one of the souks or Cairo. Deciphering its hardly readable hieroglyphs, he realized that the secret entrance within this pyramid leads to the tomb of Amenhotep II, holding the gift of the gods: The Scepter of Anubis. Trying to find it, the archeologist was going on an expedition equipped with a high-tech hieroglyph decryptor, a flashlight, and a gun, but forgetting to take a water. So, typing in the commands in form of "verb + noun", the player should help the archeologist to find the Scepter of Anubis avoiding the numerous traps and hostile pyramid's inhabitants.

175654.overview: The player must try to land a lunar landing module on the moon keeping in account fuel, velocity and distance to the surface. The game is written in BASIC.

175796.overview:
Your job as Loki is to rid the universe of the remaining Norse gods and their allies.

There are 8 waves of attackers to destroy by lining them up in the centre of the screen and then blasting them.

When you have killed enough enemy vehicles you progress to the next wave. The indicator at the bottom of the screen shows you which wave you are on.

The game begins on the ground where you have 3 waves to destroy before moving up into space for the other 5 waves.

If, at any time, you allow an enemy ship to approach too closely while it is in your sights it will destroy you. But don't despair as you can return from the underworld 4 times before being finally doomed.

Should you succeed in wiping out all 8 waves of the Viking host you may then proceed to another universe through the remaining black hole in order to perform a similar task except against a mixture of more numerous adversaries.

175852.overview: Le Fer D'Amnukor is an RPG that is the sequel to Tyrann.

175874.overview: You will find yourself on any floor of a tower which counts 60 (and a ground floor). You will know which floor you are on are and you will see yourself evolving on the plan of this floor. Your goal is to find a fabulous treasure which is located somewhere leaves in the tower... But to take the treasure, you will need to display a 4-digit secret code. If you manage to take the treasure, you will have to keep it and exit the tower.

175884.overview: A set of games that are a nice breakout with a twist. Called Le Brique a Brac on the in-game title screen.

175886.overview:
The Inca Flute is an adventure game in French. The goal is to find an Inca flute which could be the first flute of the
Andes (true legend).

175895.overview: Le Rendez Vous de la Terreur (Le Rendez-Vous de la Terreur on the title screen) is a French language horror/suspense themed text adventure with graphics for the Oric computers. It was developed by Robert Piechaud and published by ERE Informatique in 1983.

175920.overview:
Here you go in search of a priceless diamond hidden on a deserted island in the Pacific by a vanished civilization. Adventurer of lost times, you will be confronted in turn with the multiple dangers of the island (1st part of the game), and with mysterious underground passages where strange creatures roam (20th part). 

Gradually eaten away by hunger, thirst and fatigue, you will also have to be careful not to get lost among the 134 views in this game! In order to understand you, the program has a vocabulary of approximately 90 words, identified and completed instantly from the 3rd or 4th letter typed. If you type unknown orders, ORIC erases them before you even finish writing them! You also have the possibility of chaining up to 40 instructions which will then be executed automatically. Certain special instructions allow you to save a game on K7 in order to resume it later (when you arrive
in the 2nd part of the game, you will NECESSARY to make a save in order to be able, in the future, to access this part directly without going through the 1st).

175921.overview: Le Général (The General) is a managerial strategy game set in a fictional underdeveloped Latin American country. Breaking news say that after the revolution in San Théodoros, the General Tapioca, the infamous tyrant, is on the run, and the country is on fire and blood... Actually, the game is available for one or up to 9 players, which are trying to be this general. Starting with a certain budget, each turn the player should make such financial decisions for National Defense, Agriculture, Environment, Foreign Trade, Foreign Policy, Industrial Sector, Education, Transport, and Leisure, which will not lead to the anarchy and his death. In the end of each turn, the player may also throw some money to the Public Sector and Social Help. One turn is equal to one year in power. Single-player and multi-player modes have their own specifics.

175923.overview:
The Secret of the Tomb is an adventure game, written in machine language. In this game you play as an archaeologist looking for a stone miraculous hidden in an Aztec pyramid.

But to finally hold this fabulous stone in your hands, you will have to face terrible trials, fight against
demonic creatures guardians of the sacred place, overcome the countless traps, and above all uncover the secret of mysterious tomb.

175925.overview: Lotoriciels is an Italian language miscellaneous game, developed and published by Loriciels, which was released in Europe in 1984. It is intended to help create lottery playlists with the Oric Atmos and print these out. It also helps generate number forecasts based on previous lottery picks.

183927.overview: Acheron's Rage is an shoot 'em up game with some resemblances to games like Asteroids and Omega Race. It was developed and published by Softek, which was released in Europe in 1983.

183932.overview: Land of Illusion is an Adventure game, published by Tansoft, which was released in Europe in 198

421484.overview: Le Tresor du Pirate (translates to The Pirate Treasure) is a French language text adventure for the Oric-1/Atmos computers. It was devleoped by Laurent G. and published by Free Game Blot in 1984

439831.overview:
Unlike Asteroids from Arctic Computing, the Durell Software game of the same name is NOT a clone of the arcade classic, rather it's a game in which you must avoid crashing into asteroids for as long as you can without getting killed. The game was coded entirely in BASIC by Robert White and released in 1983 (the same year as the Arctic Computing game).

The game was released as part of a compilation pack with Lunar Lander.
